issues.legal_issue: A notification making a railway administration liable for tax on buildings and lands encompasses a consolidated tax assessed as a rate on buildings and lands when that consolidated tax replaces multiple municipal taxes.
material_facts: The municipality replaced the separate house tax and water rate with a consolidated tax assessed as a rate on buildings and lands.
A government notification made the railway administration liable for tax on buildings and lands within the municipality.
The notification followed correspondence in which the provincial government asked that the railway be made liable for the consolidated tax imposed in place of the house tax.
The railway paid the consolidated tax, and the Union brought a suit seeking its refund; the Union appealed after the High Court dismissed the suit.
issues.conclusion: The notification covered the consolidated tax, so the railway was liable to pay it and the municipality had collected it lawfully. The appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 135(1) of the Indian Railways Act, 1890, the government could make a railway administration liable for specified local taxes. Sections 59(1) and its second proviso clause (c) of the Bombay District Municipal Act, 1901, and Section 73(1) and its second proviso clause (c) of the Bombay Municipal Boroughs Act, 1925, permitted a consolidated tax assessed as a rate on buildings or lands in lieu of specified separate taxes. A consolidated tax assessed in that way is a tax on buildings and lands for purposes of a notification describing the liability in those terms. The Court relied on Borough Municipality, Ahmedabad v. Ahmedabad Manufacturing and Calico Printing Co. Ltd. for the analogous principle that a tax imposed in the form of a rate assessed on buildings and lands is not distinct from a rate on buildings or lands, and referred to Raza Buland Sugar Co. Ltd. v. Municipal Board, Rampur concerning the character of a water rate. It distinguished Municipal Council, Cuddappah v. M. and S. M. Ry. Co. Ltd. as turning on different statutory language and noted that Patel Gordhandas Hargovindas v. Municipal Commissioner, Ahmedabad provided little assistance.

issues.definition: When an appeal in a refund suit concerns a consolidated municipal tax that replaced separate taxes and was assessed on buildings or lands, a notification making the railway liable for buildings-or-lands tax covers that consolidated tax when it followed a request to impose that liability.
